items.original_context: Module theory: free left R-module over a unital ring with an R-basis, equivalently a direct sum R^{(I)} of copies of R, possibly infinite rank.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: For a unital associative ring R, a left R-module F is free if it has a basis B such that every element f∈F has a unique finite expansion f=Σ_{b∈B}r_b b. Equivalently F≅⊕_{b∈B}R as a left R-module.

sources.relevance: Defines free modules and bases and proves direct-sum-of-copies equivalence.
Distinguishes free modules from projective direct summands; expresses free modules as indexed direct sums.

items.mathematical_scope_and_edge_cases: R=0: the usual basis-cardinality/rank uniqueness conclusions fail; empty basis yields zero module. This meaning is not merely finite free, projective, or locally free.

items.original_context: Module theory: quotient left R-module M/N by an R-submodule N, whose elements are additive cosets m+N with addition and R-scalar action induced by M. Includes ideal modules I/I², successive filtration quotient modules and regular-module quotients R/I; extra ring, graded, flatness, or field structure is not part of this quotient-module meaning.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: If N⊆M is a left R-submodule, define M/N to be additive cosets m+N with (m+N)+(m'+N)=(m+m')+N and r(m+N)=rm+N; the projection M→M/N is surjective R-linear with kernel N.

sources.relevance: Explicit quotient module scalar multiplication and natural surjection.
Left R-module quotient including left ideals R/I that need not define quotient rings.

items.mathematical_scope_and_edge_cases: A quotient module R/I exists for left ideal I even if I is not two-sided; quotient ring multiplication requires two-sided ideal. N=M gives the zero module.

items.original_context: Set theory: injectivity of an arbitrary map f:X→Y, meaning f(x)=f(y) implies x=y for all x,y in X; for structured maps this is the underlying-set condition.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: A function f:X→Y is injective if f(x)=f(x') implies x=x' for all x,x'∈X.

sources.relevance: States the formal injectivity condition and its contrapositive.
Independent algebra textbook definition for functions between sets.

items.mathematical_scope_and_edge_cases: An empty-domain map is automatically injective. In a general category, monomorphisms need not be exactly injective functions; specialized maps can impose additional conditions.

items.original_context: Set theory: surjective function f:X→Y whose image is the entire stated codomain Y; for module homomorphisms this is the underlying-set surjectivity of the R-linear map, independent of linearity, free domain, or choice of basis.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: A function f:X→Y is surjective if for every y∈Y there exists x∈X with f(x)=y. Surjectivity of an R-linear map R^n→M is this underlying-set condition plus the independently specified linearity.

sources.relevance: Formal codomain-based onto condition.
Range exactly equals codomain.

items.mathematical_scope_and_edge_cases: Surjective R-linear map from R^n exists exactly if its target is generated by at most n elements. If Y is empty a function X→Y exists only if X is empty; then it is surjective.

items.original_context: Category theory: f:X→Y is an isomorphism iff there exists g:Y→X with gf=id_X and fg=id_Y; no underlying-set bijectivity is assumed.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: A morphism f:X→Y in a category C is an isomorphism if there exists a morphism g:Y→X for which g∘f=1_X and f∘g=1_Y.

sources.relevance: Exact categorical two-sided inverse-morphism criterion.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: scalar extension of a commutative unital k-algebra R along field extension K/k, yielding the unital K-algebra R⊗_k K with induced multiplication (r⊗a)(s⊗b)=rs⊗ab and K-scalar structure.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: For a field extension K/k and a commutative unital k-algebra A, scalar extension yields the K-algebra A_K=A⊗_k K, with K-action through the second tensor factor, multiplication (a⊗u)(b⊗v)=ab⊗uv, and identity 1_A⊗1_K.

sources.relevance: Uses K⊗_k A for field extensions as a k-algebra base change; cited statements about geometric regularity include additional hypotheses not part of construction.

items.original_context: Order theory: supremum sup(A) of subset A⊆S, an upper bound no greater than every other upper bound when it exists.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: Let (P,≤) be a partially ordered set and A⊆P. A supremum is an element u∈P satisfying a≤u for all a∈A and u≤v for every other upper bound v of A.

sources.section: Least upper/greatest lower bounds in order-theory discussion
sources.relevance: Defines sup A within arbitrary partially ordered sets, not just real numbers.
Special case over real numbers with nonempty bounded-above A; do not promote those hypotheses to arbitrary posets.

items.mathematical_scope_and_edge_cases: If A=∅, sup∅ exists iff P has a least element. In an arbitrary poset sup A may fail to exist even for nonempty A; a maximal bound is not necessarily least.

items.original_context: Category theory: hom-collection Hom_C(X,Y) of arrows X→Y; a preadditive category requires these collections to be sets carrying abelian group structures, without requiring all objects to form a set.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: For objects X,Y of a category C, Hom_C(X,Y) denotes the collection of all arrows X→Y. When C is locally small each such Hom-collection is a set; in a large-category foundational framework it may require an explicit class-level interpretation.

items.original_context: Polynomial algebra: a nonzero univariate polynomial f(X)=a_nX^n+⋯+a_0 over a commutative unital coefficient ring is monic if its leading coefficient a_n equals the multiplicative identity 1, including degree zero unit polynomial 1.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: Let R be a commutative ring with identity and let f(T)∈R[T] be a nonzero polynomial having a leading coefficient a_n at degree n. The polynomial is monic if a_n=1_R.

sources.section: Leading coefficient and monic polynomial definition
sources.relevance: A polynomial is monic when its leading coefficient equals one; zero polynomial excluded from usual leading-coefficient presentation.
Nonzero polynomial coefficient/degree and constant polynomial conventions.

items.original_context: Algebraic geometry: distinguished principal open D(f)={p∈Spec(R):f∉p} of a commutative ring's affine spectrum.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: For a commutative ring R and f∈R, the distinguished principal open D(f)⊆Spec(R) is {p∈Spec(R):f∉p}, the complement of V((f)).

sources.relevance: Defines affine spectrum, V(T), and D(f) by prime ideal containment.

items.mathematical_scope_and_edge_cases: D(0)=∅, D(1)=Spec(R), D(fg)=D(f)∩D(g); D(f) as an affine open scheme is a further structure, not the definition of the underlying open subset.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: product IJ of two ideals of a commutative unital ring R, generated by finite sums of pairwise products; ordinary ideal powers I^n for n≥1 by repeated ideal multiplication, and by convention I^0=R when nonnegative exponents are used.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: For ideals I,J of a commutative ring R, IJ is the ideal generated by products ab with a∈I and b∈J, equivalently all finite sums of such products. For n≥1, I^n is the n-fold product, and in a unital ring I^0=R is a commonly adopted convention.

sources.relevance: Explicit product ideal generated by pairwise products and positive powers of ideals.

items.mathematical_scope_and_edge_cases: The set of individual products need not be an ideal: finite sums are necessary. Positive powers are source-defined; exponent zero is a stated convention rather than silently attributed to this specific definition.

items.original_context: Commutative algebra: kernel ideal of a unital homomorphism φ:A→B of commutative rings, consisting of all a∈A mapped to 0_B; for a polynomial evaluation map it is the ideal of polynomial relations, and for a quotient-localization composite it is the inverse image of zero in the target ring.
items.term: Kernel ideal of a ring homomorphism
items.source_backed_draft_definition: For a unital ring homomorphism φ:R→S between commutative rings, ker φ={r∈R:φ(r)=0_S}; it is an ideal of R. For surjective φ the quotient R/ker φ is canonically isomorphic to S.

sources.relevance: Defines the kernel, establishes it is an ideal, and states the homomorphism theorem.

items.mathematical_scope_and_edge_cases: Kernel is set-theoretic preimage of zero, but is a submodule or ideal because φ preserves operations. Zero target is permitted under the unital zero-ring convention; the kernel then equals R.

items.original_query: direct sum ⊕_i M_i of a family of modules
items.original_context: Module theory: direct sum ⊕_{i∈I} M_i of left R-modules, the module of families (m_i) of finite support with componentwise addition and scalar multiplication, distinct from their unrestricted product.
items.source_backed_draft_definition: For an indexed family (M_i)_{i∈I} of left R-modules, their direct sum ⊕_{i∈I} M_i is the set of tuples (m_i) having finite support {i:m_i≠0}, equipped with componentwise addition and scalar multiplication.

sources.relevance: Defines arbitrary indexed module direct sum and its relation to finite products.
Explicit finite-support tuples and componentwise operations.

items.mathematical_scope_and_edge_cases: Index set I=∅ gives zero module. For finite I, direct sum and product coincide; for infinite I they can differ. Free modules are one special direct sum type, not general synonym.
